title: Fibre dimension along a specialization from a component point
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a scheme morphism and $U\subset T$ an open such that $f|_U$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $x\in X$ and $x\prime\in X$ with $f(x),f(x\prime)\in U$ and $x\prime\leadsto x$. Suppose that $x$, as a point of its ordinary fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], is generic [def-sc-generic-point] in an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Then $\dim_{x\prime}X_{f(x\prime)}=\dim_xX_{f(x)}$, with local dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] defined using open neighbourhoods.

source.place: Tag 054U, Lemma 37.22.10, specialization of a fibre component generic point; proof via Tag 054T.

proof.text: Apply the upstream open-neighbourhood theorem to x using hx and hcomponent. Since x′ specializes to x, every open neighbourhood of x contains x′ (Specializes.mem_open). Apply its constant-dimension clause at x′. The upstream theorem has no hypothesis hx′; the unchanged mathematical node, which permits that additional redundant hypothesis, follows immediately.

lean.statement:
theorem fibre_dimension_eq_of_specializes_component_restrict
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T) (U : T.Opens)
    [Flat (f ∣_ U)] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f ∣_ U)]
    (x x' : X) (hx : f x ∈ U) (hsp : x' ⤳ x)
    (hcomponent : f.asFiber x ∈ genericPoints (f.fiber (f x))) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber x') = topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber x)
